tells: B's sink is a bare rectangular cutout in the counter slab showing a wood-grain plane at the bottom instead of a stainless basin with drain, radius corners, and specular rim (A shows a real undermount stainless bowl with brushed reflections).
B's dishwasher is a featureless brushed-grey slab with no control panel, logo, badge, seam, or door gap; A's has a black control strip, indicator LEDs, brand text, and a real door reveal.
A generic white cylinder sits on B's counter with no contact shadow or reflection on the glossy quartz; the chair base and shelving units in B also sit on the carpet with no contact occlusion.
B's task lamp shade is a uniformly glowing white block with no hot spot, no warm halo on the wall, and no gradient across the shade; A's lamp has a warm falloff on the shade and a spill on the wall.

B's ceiling has a huge disk fixture with a dead-flat matte ceiling, no bloom, no highlight roll-off, and hard identical CG downlights; there is no grain anywhere, no lens softness at edges, carpet pattern is razor sharp to the far wall.

B's furniture reads as untextured box primitives: the shelving unit by the bed is floating clusters of cubes with no legs, plinth, or hardware; the bed is a generic low-poly mattress with no linens sag or headboard; the red chair has no seat cushion deformation.

A carries real-world evidence B lacks: stucco wall texture, smudges on the electrical panel, a paint edge where the wall meets the ceiling, subtle vignette and noise in the ceiling, window overexposure with blinds and a PTAC unit visible.
critics.biggestGap: The kitchenette sink in B: it is a rectangular hole in the countertop with a wood-grain plane at the bottom and no basin geometry at all. It needs to become a stainless undermount bowl like A's, with radiused corners, a raised rim/edge under the quartz, a drain and strainer, brushed-metal anisotropic reflections picking up the ceiling light, and a chrome faucet whose base actually meets the counter with a contact shadow. Right now the sink is the single object that announces "3D model" from across the room.
secondaryGaps: Dishwasher and cabinet fronts: add the black control strip, brand badge, door gap/reveal, and handle shadows seen in A; the current featureless brushed-grey panel and flush wood doors have no seams or hardware detail.

Contact shadows and ambient occlusion: the counter cylinder, chair base, shelving units, bed plinth, and wardrobe all float; every object needs a dark occluded band where it meets the carpet or quartz, and the glossy quartz should show a faint reflection of the cylinder and lamp.

Lighting model: replace the flat uniform disk fixture with a real luminaire (diffuser bloom, hot center, soft ceiling wash), give the desk lamp a warm hot spot and wall spill like A's, and let the window in the far room blow out with light spilling onto the bed and carpet; add exposure vignette, grain in shadows, and slight lens softness toward the frame edges.

Furniture fidelity: the shelving/cube unit near the bed must be a real casegood with plinth, back panel, laminate edge banding and shadows inside cubbies; the bed needs a headboard, bedding with folds and weight, and the chair needs a cushion crease and real caster geometry.

Surface wear and seams: A shows stucco wall texture, a paint line at the ceiling, a smudged electrical panel and tile grout; B is uniformly clean plaster with no wall texture, no grout lines, no baseboard shadow, and a carpet pattern that is too crisp and uniformly saturated to the far wall.
